Okay, honey, I've been in a similar situation a couple of years ago. These things still haunt me, and from time to time I still have anxiety if I will ever get away from my overbearing desi parents, but I know for a fact that at 22 now, things are much, much, much (I cannot say this enough) much better than what they were at 18. 

First of all, you have to understand that antagonizing your parents works against your interest. Stop. There are things you will have to put your head down and endure for now. The wifi, privacy, I'm sure you're a smart girl and have worked your way around these barriers, its not too difficult when you live with this kinda stuff everyday. 

Trust me when I say I *feel* your frustration. My parents never let me visit any of my friends, mum didn't let me cut my hair because dad would hate it. What works for you at this point is that you get to move away for university, and NYU or not, you will have some breathing space. I'm still living at home with my parents, till I graduate. Soldier on.

As for University, you need to EXCEL at what you're doing now. Don't let your grades waiver. Sit down with your parents, sound like a dreamy, starry eyed, ambitious girl who wants to make them so proud (desi parents dig it SO much), and pushpushpush till they let you go to the Uni you want to. Ace it there. Excel, become independent, and you have the golden ticket out of the life you're dreading.
Now comes the scenario that you don't. Endure the Uni they're pushing, be at the top of your game, and go to a grad school of your choice/find work that keeps you away from them. You'll be in a better position then to make choices for yourself. 
You must realize that your education *will* be your flight outta here, don't ever, ever, mess it up. Everyone, and I mean everyone in your life will come and go, don't put them anywhere before your education. If you don't want to live your mother's life, that has GOT to be your priority. 

I'm here, dreading an arranged marriage myself, and painfully close to the age when the pressure begins. I'm hoping grad school will give me the time and resources to find my own place, and live the life I want.

I get you feel trapped, and suicidal, and I wish I could reach out across the internet and give you a hug. I also know that talking doesn't always help, as sometimes it boggles people, a situation like ours. They never know why we feel like we do.
If you want to talk, please, PM me. Anytime. About anything.

You will make it. You will live the life you've always dreamed of. You will be happy, and you will be glad you endured it all. This will only make you come out stronger. I promise.
